title: Flat finitely presented morphisms of spaces are universally open
statement: Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat and locally of finite presentation. Then $f$ is universally open: for every morphism $Y'\to Y$ of algebraic spaces, the map $|X\times_YY'|\to|Y'|$ is open [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The topology on an algebraic space is the quotient topology from any surjective etale scheme atlas. In particular $|f|(|X|)$ is open in $|Y|$.

proof.text: Choose scheme atlases of X and Y from def-trf-algebraic-space. Test the target atlas over the composite of the source atlas with f. The resulting scheme U has a compatible map h to the target atlas V. Surjectivity of the projection U to the original source atlas follows by uniqueness of representing pullback squares; use Yoneda to transfer their isomorphism to schemes. Scheme base change proves that a surjective etale scheme morphism induces a representable surjective etale Yoneda map. Compose with the source atlas using isEtale_comp and direct pasting of surjective scheme tests.
Apply the flatness and local-finite-presentation chart tests to h. Mathlib UniversallyOpen.of_flat proves that h is universally open.

For every algebraic-space base change Yprime to Y, choose a scheme atlas W to Yprime. Test V to Y over W to form Z, and form the scheme fibre product T = U times_V Z. The scheme map T to Z is universally open, and Z to W is etale, so T to W is open. Construct T to P = X times_Y Yprime by the presheaf pullback universal properties. Pullback pasting exhibits this map as a composite of base changes of the atlas of X and the atlas W; direct scheme tests prove it representable etale and surjective. Reuse the existing representableWith_baseChange helper of lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence for both properties, exposed in its original module rather than reproved here.

A representable surjective scheme-source map is surjective on point classes: test on each field-valued representative, lift the field point to the representing surjective scheme map, and take its residue field. The definition of the final point topology makes every etale scheme-source map continuous. The affine-atlas topology theorem gives a topology tau in which all etale scheme-source maps are open and continuous; compare the defining supremum with tau and the coinduced topology of its atlas to identify tau with the existing point topology. Functoriality of schemePointMap along a scheme morphism follows from naturality of residue-field maps and Quot.sound. Hence the composite |T| to |P| to |Yprime| equals the open composite |T| to |W| to |Yprime|. Apply IsOpenMap.of_comp to the continuous surjective map |T| to |P|. This proves universal openness without identifying topological fibre products.

For the identity base change, compare the range of its second projection on points with the range of f using the first projection and the canonical section into the pullback. Quotient induction proves functoriality of mapPoint and identifies pointImage with its range. Apply universal openness to the full open subset, obtaining the asserted open whole image. Empty sources and empty opens are covered by the same argument.
